anchors.name: cohn_elkies_bound_dim_8
anchors.derivation: Cohn and Elkies, New upper bounds on sphere packings I, Annals of Mathematics 157 (2003), Table 3, page 711, column 'New Upper Bound', row 8. Centre density. Read from the paper.

anchors.name: best_packing_known_dim_12
anchors.derivation: Same table, column 'Best Packing Known', row 12. Used as the floor: a certified bound below it would contradict an exhibited packing and is reported rather than scored.

anchors.name: rogers_bound_dim_12
anchors.derivation: Same table, column "Rogers' Bound", row 12. Reported as a milestone, not used as a score anchor: Rogers comes from a different technique and no exactly certifiable submission has reached it at any degree tried here.

anchors.name: optimal_centre_density_dim_8
anchors.derivation: Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension eight: the optimum is exactly 1/16, attained by E8, and the Cohn-Elkies linear programming bound is tight there. This is what makes dimension 8 the rung with a known answer.

anchors.name: three_point_bound_dim_4
anchors.derivation: Cohn, de Laat and Salmon, Three-point bounds for sphere packing: 0.125 <= delta_4 <= 0.12891. Recorded because it shows the two-point linear programming bound this task certifies is no longer the strongest known technique in low dimensions, which is a live line of work and the reason the anchors carry retrieval dates.
